content.title: About
content.content: White Russian is a classic cocktail made of vodka, coffee liqueur (usually Kahlúa) and cream. It originated in the United States in the mid‑20th century and gained widespread popularity after appearing in the film "The Big Lebowski". The drink is smooth and creamy with coffee and alcohol notes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded White Russian recipe appeared in 1965 at the Metropole bar in London.
It became a cult favorite after the 1998 movie "The Big Lebowski", where the main character drinks it frequently.
Many variations exist, including the Black Russian (no cream) and the Colorado Bulldog (with cola).
For a lighter version, milk is often used instead of cream.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Coffee liqueur provides a small amount of caffeine, which can increase alertness.

items.title: Calcium from cream
items.content: Cream supplies calcium, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vodka and coffee liqueur contain modest amounts of B‑vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: White Russian contains a notable amount of alcohol; consume responsibly.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Cream and coffee liqueur make the drink calorie‑dense, which can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream may cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of certain medications; caution is advised when taking drugs.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: White Russian is served in a lowball (old‑fashioned) glass over ice. First pour vodka and coffee liqueur, then gently add cream, allowing it to swirl through the drink. Stir lightly before sipping.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the components separately: vodka and coffee liqueur in a cool, dark place; cream in the refrigerator and use within a few days after opening.
